summary_en: Implemented Fenix-owned OCI execution isolation with measured synthetic-account tests; production migration and stronger-runtime adoption remain separate.
summary_es: Aislamiento OCI propio implementado y probado con cuentas sintéticas; la migración de producción y los runtimes más fuertes quedan separados.
workspace_state: Pre-existing uncommitted work preserved. Hashes identify selected implementation files, not a clean committed release.

environment.test_image_role: Existing local image supplies OS tools and Chromium; not a rebuilt/deployed final controller image.
environment.tests_run_as: Normal developer user for Rust/policy tests; explicit sudo for disposable Docker, AppArmor and filesystem tests.

acceptance_matrix_note: Mapping to the 33 original targets. Partial or bounded-scope entries are not claims of complete acceptance. These are regression fixtures, not a proof of security or an independent penetration test.

acceptance_matrix.evidence: Gateway tenant-routing tests and authenticated service owner-spoof rejection.
Owner-filtered execution/checkpoint lists and private marketplace rows tested; not an exhaustive enumeration of every UI count.
Gateway restart, registry reorder, stable identity and fixed expiry regression test.
Real HTTP quiet-stream revocation, re-enable rejection, credential/revision checks and runner revocation.
Foreign runner status/cancel, browser CDP connection and checkpoint deletion denied; no exhaustive browser artifact-ID matrix.
Existing project/subagent/scheduler/Telegram regressions pass and use the shared execution context; no real multi-account Telegram or delayed production-job drill.
Native broker denies foreign connection IDs before dispatch. Universal MCP/OAuth refresh adapters are not implemented.
Existing immutable public snapshot/private owner report marketplace regressions pass.
Real shell environment/mount secrecy, PTY, read-only offline language-server launch and browser mounts tested. Real pylsp protocol test remains opt-in.
Descriptor-relative traversal/link rejection, pinned inode path replacement, archive links and authenticated restore fixtures pass.
Policy rejects overlapping writable tasks and foreign workspace mounts. A prolonged simultaneous multi-account write stress test was not run.
Full firewall rules verified; a controlled host listener is unreachable from the runner. Metadata, public NAT hairpin and every other-account port were not probed end-to-end.
IPv6 disabled in runner configuration; broker rejects private/mixed DNS and configured host/NAT addresses. No exhaustive live rebinding/redirect adversary test.
Packet rules constrain protocols and ports independently of client proxy behavior; real host TCP denial verified. UDP/QUIC saturation probes not run.
Empty policy rejected in unit fixture; live guard reconciliation and complete verification pass. Process interruption midway through iptables-restore not injected.
Startup gates, controller lifetime binding and monitoring implemented. No host reboot or Docker daemon restart drill; polling is not zero-latency enforcement.
Mandatory execution transport fails closed, configured runtime must exist, and Docker cancellation failure reports pending cleanup while killing the cgroup.
Fixed HTTPS host/port/method/path and pinned TLS destination implemented. Live API/SNI mismatch matrix not executed.
Current account revision, runner revocation and disabled-owner checkpoint restore covered; live external write revocation race not exercised.
Bounded JSON response, redirect/secret-reflection rejection and restricted audit fields implemented. No live adversarial credential-echo service test.
Foreign integration and caller resource/body-field overrides rejected; durable usage budget tested with synthetic API transport.
Registry duplicates/insecure permissions rejected; real controller provisioning/preflight confirms UID, image, mounts, quotas, token and revision.
Real cgroup memory/PID settings and account slices verified; full CPU/RAM/fork/descriptor-pressure fairness drill not performed.
Actual fixed-size ext4 ENOSPC, remount and migration tested; snapshot bounds and bounded logging/metadata implemented. Combined multi-account host exhaustion not run.
Real detached descendants disappear on cancellation; one-use attach and direct cgroup stop during a synthetic Docker API failure verified.
Actual Chromium inner sandbox and authenticated owner-scoped CDP work; browser-only mounts verified. Full adversarial navigation/profile matrix remains opt-in.
Existing design preview isolation retained; frontend browser security matrix not rerun in this task.
No public preview grants introduced. Private runner port connections require current owner authorization; foreign CDP denied.
Disabled owner cannot restore; ciphertext tampering fails before destination creation.
Encrypted project-file restore/clone produces fresh directories/generations. RAM snapshots and warm-machine reassignment are not implemented.
File restoration does not replay APIs; broker has no automatic retry and failed/ambiguous calls consume usage. No live payment/write rollback test.
Audit is outside runner mounts, private, rotated and excludes raw secrets/arguments. Full host incident/tamper drill not executed.

Shell, terminal, skill helper, isolated language-server process, Chromium/CDP and file restore tested. Final image deployment, real external APIs and complete UI download flow remain deployment checks.

validation_notes: An initial all-target link exhausted disk; only regenerable Cargo incremental cache was removed.
A default-parallel test exceeded an existing five-second runtime assertion under load. Final all-target run uses two test threads; that timing assertion was not weakened.

Stale tests assuming a fixed skill count, full upfront skill catalog and former browser authorization wording were aligned with the existing on-demand behavior. Two existing Clippy findings were simplified without behavior changes.
No paid provider request or real external integration write was made. Frontend files were not changed by this security implementation.
Shared host-kernel isolation, host root/Docker authority and polling detection latency remain explicit trust/operational limits. File checkpoints are not atomic RAM/block snapshots.

upstream_reuse.adaptation: Constrained user/PID/network namespace operations and chroot for the Chromium inner sandbox.
Named Fenix browser policy with user namespace permission; mount/proc/sys restrictions retained.
